description.narrative: India faces a significant issue with protein deficiency, particularly in rural areas. Protein-rich foods remain underutilised, not necessarily because they are scarce, but due to a mix of cultural preferences, limited nutritional awareness, and financial constraints. The last decade, different organisations have tried to tackle this problem by introducing tempeh into the market, a product that is high in protein, low in cost and that could fit well into the Indian cooking culture. In different regions in India tempeh is now successfully being introduced in local communities, while creating jobs and improving access to high protein food. Although some successes are there, challenges, especially in terms of upscaling, do exists. Therefore the project purpose is two-fold: • Complete an ecosystem analyses of India’s tempeh sector to better understand the local consumption patterns and food culture, and have an overview of the stakeholders and their roles in the tempeh value chain; and • Draft a roadmap describing how tempeh consumption and production can be upscaled with the goal to increase the access to this affordable food high in nutrition and protein, specifically among the poorer communities in India, while contributing to more decent jobs for the rural communities.
